title: Deploy and run the queue coverage reconciliation from #7016

labels.name: effort/m
labels.description: Medium: expected under 1 day of work

body:
## Problem

PR #7697 added the queue coverage endpoint, reconciliation script, hourly persistent systemd units, and registry entry, but its PR body leaves the first-run acceptance pending: the units were not installed and the running broker returned `unknown command /coverage`. Current state still shows `queue-coverage-reconcile.timer` as not found/inactive for this user session. Issue #7016 is closed, but the scheduled first-run coverage result has not been recorded.

## Acceptance

- The broker serving the laptop queue accepts the `/coverage` request used by `scripts/fleet/queue-reconcile/check_coverage.py`; failures continue to report an error instead of a false zero.
- The service/timer are installed through the declarative user-service path and enabled; the hourly persistent timer matches the existing `doc/fleet-schedule-registry.md` entry.
- Run the script in observe mode against the four pilot repos. If it reports uncovered issues or ready PRs, use the sanctioned import path to create their live pilot tasks, then rerun until the report shows zero uncovered work or explicitly records a remaining state with live task coverage.
- Save the first verified report and read back that the timer is enabled and active.

## Evidence

- PR #7697's body says the first run was pending deployment, the units were uninstalled, and the running broker returned `unknown command /coverage`.
- On 2026-11-25, `systemctl --user is-enabled queue-coverage-reconcile.timer` returned `not-found` and `is-active` returned `inactive`.
- No existing open issue or queued pilot task for installing/running this coverage reconciliation was found.

## Scope

Deploy the already-shipped #7016 mechanism and verify its first complete run. Do not change the queue matching or coverage semantics without a separate decision.
